description: QuinLED dig2go single-output WS281x controller in a closed case. Probed on the desk 2026-08-06: ESP32-D0WD-V3 revision v3.1, 4 MB flash, CH34x USB bridge enumerating as 1a86:7523. Pin facts agree between the vendor pinout guide and QuinLED's own WLED build config (platformio_override.ini in intermittech/QuinLED-Firmware): LED data GPIO16 on the pigtail, touch button GPIO0, LED power relay enable GPIO12. GPIO12 carries two roles at once: it gates the LED supply (the vendor's "custom relay" circuit cuts LED power completely when off, and the header's 5 V is switched with it), and it is MTDI, the classic-ESP32 flash-voltage strap — high at boot selects 1.8 V VDD_SDIO and the board does not boot, so it must be low at boot and only asserted afterwards. It is declared here as a reserved GPIO plus a power_gate entry, never as a claimable wire; un-asserted, the strip is dark rather than dim. UART0 (GPIO1/3) runs the CH340 host link and the LED wiring does not touch it. Pins the case does not expose are omitted rather than guessed (boards/README.md): the IR receiver on GPIO5 and the ICS-43434 microphone (SD 19 / WS 4 / SCK 18), which LightPlayer registers no driver for, and GPIO21/22/23/25, which the vendor's pinout guide lists on a dupont header but which are not verified on this unit.

board_label.label: LED
board_label.note: the LED pigtail/connector — the board's only LED output, level-shifted, and powered through the GPIO12 gate

gpio.reserved_reason: capacitive touch button on the case, and the BOOT strapping pin; not exposed as an output
UART0 TX into the CH340 bridge — the host serial link; driving it drops the link
UART0 RX from the CH340 bridge — the host serial link; driving it drops the link
LED power gate (see power_gate) + MTDI flash-voltage strap — must be low at boot (high selects 1.8 V VDD_SDIO and the board will not boot); never claimable as a wire

power_gate.note: Feeds is deliberately empty: this gate switches the board's only LED supply, so it gates every output. Pre-walk placeholders, both to be measured and confirmed on the bench before this board ships to users: active-high is inferred from the vendor calling GPIO12 the "LED Relay enable pin" of a solid-state "custom relay" circuit (assert to enable), and 25 ms is a chosen settle time, not a measured one. Rail-off is also the strap-safe boot state, since GPIO12 is MTDI and must be low at reset.
